user_questions.question: Who should receive the low-stock alert: (a) the storefront's Primary Contact (Storefront__c.Primary_Contact__c, set on all 21 storefronts, 10 distinct contacts with email, none a Salesforce user), (b) the storefront record owner (today one System Administrator owns all 21), or (c) both? Recommendation: (a).
user_questions.simulated_answer: Alert the storefront's Primary Contact when stock is below the threshold.

skill_friction: AskCoworker returned three wrong claims (D2: validation rules and LWC 'not SOQL-queryable'; R: '10 emails per transaction' for flow Send Email). The two-wrong-claims rule applied; the SKILL gives no guidance on how to classify an AskCoworker platform-limit claim like the 10-per-transaction one that cannot be tested read-only.

R and T both timed out at ~60s with the standard 400-word templates even though the inventory had 12 rows; the 'more than 8 changes -> API names only and split R' guidance helped only after the timeout. The templates' default limits seem too large for this service.
validate_spec.py exits with code 1 even when ok=true and the file is saved, which looks like a failure to a runner.

Unclear whether 'who gets alerted' is a persona question (ask) or delivery implementation (decide); I asked because the owner (one admin) and Primary Contact (external contacts) are different audiences.
Email opt-out rule ('respect by default') conflicts in spirit with operational/transactional alerts; followed it and listed the gap as a proposal.
